newsitem.title: USA: Man in Calif. shootings seen laughing as he fired.
newsitem.headline: Man in Calif. shootings seen laughing as he fired.

text.p: Police searched on Friday for a man who walked into a McDonald's in northern California and while laughing opened fire with a revolver, injuring three of the fast-food restaurant's employees, one critically.
The unidentified gunman opened fire late on Thursday inside a McDonald's in Vallejo, about 25 miles northeast of San Francisco, injuring three female employees.

The suspect "strolled" into the restaurant, approached three women at a table, and "calmly" began shooting, Lt. Al Lehman said. The gunman, who did not speak during the attack, appeared to be laughing as he pulled the trigger, police said.
All three victims were shot in the head at close range, Lehman said. The gunman, who left the crime scene on foot through the same door he entered, did not try to steal any money from the restaurant.
"He didn't come in to rob the store," Lehman said. "He walked up to three women and shot them and walked out. It just doesn't make any sense. It's extremely bizarre, scary."

The suspect was described by police as a black male, age 29 to 33. He was wearing black pants and a black jacket with yellow and white lettering. A composite sketch of the gunman, who remained at large, was released Friday.
The injured employees were identified by police as Melanie Boncato, 17, Mercedes Manuel, 21, and Larienel Sapinoso, whose age was unknown but police said she was a junior at a local high school.
Boncato was reported in extremely critical condition. The other two victims were listed in stable condition. "At this point we have no motive," Sgt. Herman Robinson said.
